review_notes: I read the whole file and compared candidate duplicates. Within Assembly.lean the repeated pieces (symmetric/Hermitian conversion, periodicity rewrites) are short, so I did not report them. The one real duplication I found is across files. The floor-based reduction of an arbitrary point of ℝⁿ to the cube [0,2π]ⁿ appears in `exists_le_of_continuous_periodic` here and again inside `posDefSmoothMetric_stability` in RealizableMetrics.lean (about lines 634-655). I only skimmed the RealizableMetrics block, which is auto-generated style code, so the exact rewrite there is a sketch that I have not checked against Lean. I assumed `periodicShift`, `IsPeriodic2Pi` and `posDefSmoothMetric_stability` are as in the sources I read. I did not check `Periodization.lean`'s one `floor` occurrence.

findings.excerpt: set k : Fin n → ℤ := fun i => -⌊x i / (2 * Real.pi)⌋ with hk
findings.problem: The proof contains a general fact: every x : Fin n → ℝ has an integer shift k with x + periodicShift n k in [0,2π]ⁿ. Here it is proved by hand with Int.floor_le, Int.lt_floor_add_one and two nlinarith calls, and it is buried inside a bound lemma. The same floor-based reduction is redone in `posDefSmoothMetric_stability` in RealizableMetrics.lean, which Assembly.lean already imports. That second proof uses the same floor expression, the same two floor inequalities and the same `2 * Real.pi` positivity facts. So the cube reduction is proved twice, in different styles, and neither copy can be reused.
findings.proposed_change:
Add a shared lemma, next to `periodicShift` in Sobolev/Periodicity.lean or at the top of RealizableMetrics.lean: `lemma exists_periodicShift_mem_Icc (x : Fin n → ℝ) : ∃ k : Fin n → ℤ, x + periodicShift n k ∈ Set.Icc (0 : Fin n → ℝ) (fun _ => 2 * Real.pi)`. Proof: take k i = -⌊x i / (2π)⌋ and run the existing floor argument, which is lines 153-167 of this file. Then rewrite the two uses.
(1) In `exists_le_of_continuous_periodic`, the proof after obtaining `C, hC` becomes `obtain ⟨k, hmem⟩ := exists_periodicShift_mem_Icc x; have hbd := hC _ hmem; rw [hp x k] at hbd; exact ...`. The `set k`, `hpi` and `hmem` blocks disappear.
(2) In `posDefSmoothMetric_stability`, replace the `specialize hK (fun i => x i - ⌊..⌋ * (2π))` plus the two nlinarith membership goals plus the `convert ... rw [← this]; swap; exact fun i => -⌊..⌋` block with `obtain ⟨k, hk⟩ := exists_periodicShift_mem_Icc x; have := hK _ hk v hv; rwa [hg.smoothPeriodic.periodic x k] at this`. Both uses fit their hypotheses: hK is stated for all x in the cube and g is 2π-periodic via `hg.smoothPeriodic.periodic`.
findings.benefit: The fundamental-domain argument is proved once and named, so its floor and nlinarith details are not maintained twice. The remaining periodic-compactness proofs shrink to 'pick the shift, apply the cube bound, rewrite by periodicity'. Any later compactness argument on the torus, such as other uniform bounds in the assembly, can reuse the lemma without another floor computation.
